newsitem.title: UK: Hoare buys 10 mln LucasVarity shares.
newsitem.headline: Hoare buys 10 mln LucasVarity shares.

text.p: ABN AMRO Hoare Govett bought 10 million LucasVarity Plc shares on behalf of the company at 198p per share, a Hoare spokesman said.
The trade is the first in the company's programme to buy back shares starting with a three percent stock repurchase this year which could be repeated next year.
"They are declared buyers but can come and go whenever they like - whenever they think they can get them cheaply," said the Hoare spokesman.
"They have authority to buy 42 million shares and they've made a big start buying about quarter of that," he said.

This style of buy-back is more like a U.S. stock repurchase than one usually executed in the UK market and is similar to the programme done by Barclays Bank Plc earlier this year. Companies in the UK usually buy back shares all at once.
Dealers said the fall was due to unpopularity of the style of buy-back.

"People hoped they'd make a quick turn out of this if LucasVarity came in and bought the shares in a lump, so it spiked up after they said they'd do the buy-back on Tuesday and now it's coming off because they're disappointed," said a dealer.
